title: Majority parity expectation identity
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set and let $F,P:A\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\mathbb E_{a\in A}[P(a)]=0$, where expectation is uniform. For independent uniformly chosen $a,b,c\in A$,
\[
\mathbb E\left[\frac{F(a)+F(b)+F(c)-F(a)F(b)F(c)}{2}\,P(a)P(b)P(c)\right]
=-\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathbb E_{a\in A}[F(a)P(a)]\right)^3.
\]
hypotheses_covered: F and P are real-valued functions on A
The uniform mean of P is zero
